general_information.Description: Objective: The main Objective of The course is to improve economic literacy as well as critical thinking and problem solving skills to explain and predict economic issues -Description: Economics is The study of how The society manages its scarce resources. Economics has been divided into The subcategories of microeconomics and macroeconomics. While macroeconomics studies aggregate issues related to national and international economic activities, this course - microeconomics - focuses on The behavior of individual economic agents. microeconomics studies how households (or individuals), business (or firms, enterprises) and The government make decisions, given scarcity of resources. It also studies The interactions among those market members and how these interactions have impacts on their economic benefits and The economy. Because most of these activities occur in The markets, this course also focuses on how The markets work.
general_information.StudentTasks: + Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination + Read textbooks and other materials in advance before class + Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and materials of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment. + Actively participate in class activities + Complete all homework assignments and other tasks given by the instructor + Use personal laptop in class only for learning purposes + Don’t have private conversations or arrive at class late, which can disrupt the learning environment of the class

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Discuss the theory of supply and demand
Recognize the influences of market equilibrium and disequilibrium
Describe the theory of supply and demand in real-life scenarios
Identify the tools and strategies to understand supply and demand applications
Analyze the influences of aggregate demand and aggregate supply
Understand how the government policies affect individuals, firms, and society.
Understand how the fiscal and monetary policies affect macroeconomy.
Show self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context.

assessments.Note: Participation scores will be given based on students' class attendance, preparation, quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussions, and building upon others’ comments.

The PPT slides and written report of the presentation must be sent to the instructor before deadlines. Each group presentation will take place in appx. 15 minutes. The Q&A session will follow for about 10 minutes.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Individual Assignment 1 covers chapters 1 to 6; Individual Assignment 2 covers chapters 7 to 12
assessments.Grading Guide: Approach 1: homework exercises Approach 2: constructive questions, guided by instructor
assessments.Note: In some particular sessions, homework assignments will be given to students. The exercises in these assignments will cover subjects from the session when the previous assignment is handed. Students are required to do individually at home and submit to the instructor according to the deadlines.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Quiz 1 covers chapters 1 to 4; Quiz 2 covers chapters 5 to 8
assessments.Note: These quizzes are organized in the beginning of some sessions and informed to students in advance. Students have time at home for preparation. Students are not allowed to use books or documents in any form during the quizzes.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Give three examples of important trade-offs that you face in your life

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: “An increase in the demand for notebooks raises the quantity of notebooks demanded but not the quantity supplied.” Is this statement true or false? Explain.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: Does a change in consumers’ tastes lead to a movement along the demand curve or to a shift in the demand curve? Does a change in price lead to a movement along the demand curve or to a shift in the demand curve? Explain your answers.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Beer and pizza are complements because they are often enjoyed together. When the price of beer rises, what happens to the supply, demand, quantity supplied, quantity demanded, and price in the market for pizza?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: What are the supply schedule and the supply curve, and how are they related? Why does the supply curve slope upward?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: Does a change in producers’ technology lead to a movement along the supply curve or to a shift in the supply curve? Does a change in price lead to a movement along the supply curve or to a shift in the supply curve?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Give an example of a price ceiling and an example of a price floor.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: How does a tax on a good affect the price paid by buyers, the price received by sellers, and the quantity sold?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: Explain why economists usually oppose price controls.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Suppose the government removes a tax on buyers of a good and levies a tax of the same size on sellers of the good. How does this change in tax policy affect the price that buyers pay sellers for this good, the amount buyers are out of pocket (including any tax payments they make), the amount sellers receive (net of any tax payments they make), and the quantity of the good sold?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: What determines how the burden of a tax is divided between buyers and sellers? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: If the government places a $500 tax on luxury cars, will the price paid by consumers rise by more than $500, less than $500, or exactly $500? Explain.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Explain how buyers’ willingness to pay, consumer surplus, and the demand curve are related.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: Explain how sellers’ costs, producer surplus, and the supply curve are related.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: An early freeze in California sours the lemon crop. Explain what happens to consumer surplus in the market for lemons. Explain what happens to consumer surplus in the market for lemonade. Illustrate your answers with diagrams.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Explain why an economy’s income must equal its expenditure.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: Which contributes more to GDP—the production of an economy car or the production of a luxury car? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: The government purchases component of GDP does not include spending on transfer payments such as Social Security. Thinking about the definition of GDP, explain why transfer payments are excluded.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: Why do economists use real GDP rather than nominal GDP to gauge economic well-being?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Which do you think has a greater effect on the CPI: a 10 percent increase in the price of chicken or a 10 percent increase in the price of caviar? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: Over a long period of time, the price of a candy bar rose from $0.20 to $1.20. Over the same period, the CPI rose from 150 to 300. Adjusted for overall inflation, how much did the price of the candy bar change?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Would you rather live in a nation with a high level of GDP and a low growth rate or in a nation with a low level of GDP and a high growth rate?
